sections.html:
Greenwich is the southwesternmost town in Connecticut and in New England. The 2020 population was 63,518. Of its 67.2 square miles, 47.8 are land and 19.4 are water, and it borders Port Chester, Rye Brook and North Castle in New York, Stamford to the east, and Long Island Sound to the south. With that much shoreline, a waterfront seller should ask an insurance agent about the flood zone before pricing.

The town also owns offshore islands. Great Captain Island holds the southernmost point in Connecticut and has a lighthouse.

Land was bought from the Siwanoy people for the New Haven Colony in 1640, and the General Assembly made Greenwich a township on May 11, 1665. Population went from 12,172 in 1900 to 33,112 in 1930, then to 63,518 by 2020.

That growth came in waves, so a seller here may own a colonial in the historic district, a mid-century house or a newer build. Repair needs differ a lot across those eras: older houses tend to need work on systems and structure, while newer ones often need only cosmetic updates. Buyers and inspectors sort houses by age quickly, so know where yours falls.

Greenwich is one taxing body made of distinct sections, and the Census Bureau recognizes nine communities within it. Three have their own post office names and ZIP codes.

  • Cos Cob, Old Greenwich and Riverside, each with its own postal name.
  • Byram, Glenville and Pemberwick.
  • Indian Field and Rock Ridge.
  • Central Greenwich around the municipal center.

Informal areas include Belle Haven, Back Country, Banksville, Mianus and Stanwich. ZIP codes in town are 06830, 06831, 06870 and 06878. Use the neighborhood name buyers use when you describe your house, not just the postal address.

Hedge funds and financial firms cluster in Greenwich, drawn by quiet residential streets and a short ride to Manhattan. AQR Capital, Viking Global Investors, Silver Point Capital, Interactive Brokers, W. R. Berkley, XPO and Tudor Investment Corporation are based in town, and Greenwich Hospital and Eversource Energy are other large institutions.

Because so much work is in finance, many buyers come from New York and commute by rail. Grand Central is about 50 minutes on the express and 60 on a local. Westchester County Airport is about 15 minutes by car, and LaGuardia roughly 35.

Interstate 95 crosses the southern end of town with four exits, 2 through 5, and Route 1 and the Merritt Parkway also run through. Four Metro-North stations serve the town. If your house is within walking distance of one, say so early with any buyer. Amtrak trains stop in neighboring Stamford.

The public system has eleven elementary schools, three middle schools (Central, Eastern and Western) and one high school. Roughly 25 to 30 percent of K-12 students attend private schools, among them Brunswick School, Greenwich Academy and Greenwich Country Day School.

Mean daily highs run from 35 degrees in January to 82 in July, and the town gets about 50 inches of precipitation a year, with about 28 inches of snow. The area north of the Merritt Parkway gets more snow than the coast, where the Sound moderates temperatures.

Coastal homes face water and insurance questions. Inland, higher houses face winter wear on roofs and driveways. Ask your insurance agent about your lot before you list.

sections.h2: Town government and the tax collector
sections.html:
Greenwich has three selectmen elected town-wide and a Representative Town Meeting of 230 unpaid members that must approve every budget. Each voter picks only two of the three selectmen, which nearly always produces a split board. The town runs its own public safety, with career firefighters plus eight all-volunteer fire companies, and the police department is at 11 Bruce Place.

All neighborhoods share one tax base, so the tax collector is the single point of contact when you need a payoff figure for any unpaid property tax at closing.

Greenwich has four town beaches on the Sound: Greenwich Point, Byram Beach, Island Beach and Great Captain Island. Access was long limited to residents until the Connecticut Supreme Court ruled in Leydon v. Greenwich in 2001 and the town changed its policy for all four.

  • Binney Park, Bruce Park, Cos Cob Park and Byram Park.
  • Mianus River Park and the Babcock Preserve.
  • Calf Island, a 29-acre island about 3,000 feet off Byram, with a bird sanctuary on its west side.

The Bruce Museum is town-owned, and Putnam Cottage is a historic house museum.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and state tax
sections.html:
Under section 12-497, a Greenwich deed sits unrecorded at the town clerk's office until the tax return is in and the tax is paid. Section 12-494 builds the charge from two pieces: three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-fourth of one percent to the town. For residential sales of $800,000 or more, the state rate climbs on the slice above $800,000, then again above $2.5 million.

The 2026 Supplement holds recent amendments. Have your closing attorney confirm the figures before you rely on any estimate, and expect the payment to come out of your proceeds at the closing table.

sections.h2: If you owe property tax at closing
sections.html:
Unpaid town tax does not stop a sale. The balance is a lien that the closing attorney finds in the title search, and it is paid from your proceeds before you receive anything. Ask the tax collector for a payoff figure close to the closing date, since interest keeps running until the day it is paid.

The same goes for a mortgage. Request a payoff statement in writing, hand it to the attorney, and expect the deed to be recorded only after those balances are cleared and the conveyance tax is paid.

Listing a Greenwich house can reach a wide pool of buyers. A house needing work, or a sale with a deadline, may suit a cash buyer better, since a cash buyer purchases as-is and does not depend on a lender's appraisal.

  • Listing: broader exposure, more showings, inspection requests.
  • Cash sale: simpler, driven by title work, usually at a discount to a renovated sale.

Get any offer in writing and have your attorney review the contract before you sign. Pull together the deed, your tax bill and any payoff statement now, so title work can begin the day you say yes.

faqs.q: Is Greenwich the largest town on the Gold Coast?
faqs.a: It is described as the largest town on Connecticut's Gold Coast, in southwestern Fairfield County, with a 2020 population of 63,518.

faqs.q: How long is the train from Greenwich to Manhattan?
faqs.a: Metro-North's New Haven Line takes about 50 minutes to Grand Central on the express and about 60 on the local.

faqs.q: Do I pay conveyance tax when selling a Greenwich house?
faqs.a: Connecticut taxes deeds of $2,000 or more, with higher state rates on residential sales above $800,000. Ask your closing attorney for the current figure.

faqs.q: How many public high schools does Greenwich have?
faqs.a: One. Greenwich High School is the sole high school, with three middle schools feeding it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greenwich house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases the house in its current condition, with no repairs. Compare offers in writing and have a contract reviewed before signing.
